title: Wellman Braud, who called him 'Millet'
summary: Millet is a New Orleans nickname used between him and Braud, who became his best friend and guided him in New York and in Duke's band.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: You mentioned in New York that Wellman Braud called you Millet, Miyai?
Millet.
Millet. How do you spell -- ?
I don't know how you spell it. It's --
Millet.
Millet. That's a nickname for anybody, I guess, from New Orleans.
Oh.
See, I didn't know Braud in New Orleans

at all, only when I -- I knew he was from New Orleans when I got to New York because somebody had told him about this boy from New Orleans in the band with King Oliver, and all that, so he came over and we got acquainted. He got to be my best friend. He looked out for me in New York. I mean, because he had been in New York long years, and he looked out for me and he saw that nothing would happen to me. In fact, he guided me right. He was like my father, you know. And we were real thick, real thick friends.
Was it he who started calling you Millet?
Yeah, Millet.
Millet?
Millet. Hey, Millet.
I remember we got to Duke's band -- and that's one thing I didn't think Duke liked because he didn't know what we were talking about half of the time.
(Laughing.)
So --
Did you have any other nickname?
No, that's all I had. "Snake Charmer" was the main one, and that was the main one, and Millet was -- that was between Braud and I.
But I did all right, though, in -- I enjoyed -- I used to play -- Honest to God, I played parades from nine
o'clock in the morning till five in the evening for 75 cents, walking. And when I'd get home, I'd get a tub of hot water to soak my feet in and go right to bed. Boy, --
